title: Correct the SLA endpoint percentile boundary
prompt:
Correct the off-by-one percentile selection in the public provider SLA response. Evidence: src/app/api/v1/bazaar/providers/[id]/sla/route.ts:50-53 sorts valid positive latency samples, but lines 59-61 index the array with floor(length * 0.95). For twenty ordered samples from 1 through 20 milliseconds, execution of the actual GET handler returned p95_latency_ms=20. Under the nearest-rank definition, the nineteenth observation is the 95th percentile; the maximum is currently reported instead at this exact rank boundary.

Change only src/app/api/v1/bazaar/providers/[id]/sla/route.ts in production. Use the zero-based nearest-rank index ceil(sampleCount * 0.95) - 1 for a nonempty sorted sample set, documenting that definition locally. Preserve empty-sample behavior, existing latency filtering, average calculation, and all other response fields. Keep this a single SLA reporting correction; do not change the separate trust-score formula or introduce a shared production helper.

Add tests/provider-sla-p95.test.mjs using a mocked Supabase query chain and NextResponse adapter to execute the real GET handler. Test unordered twenty- and hundred-sample fixtures, one sample, repeated values, no samples, and excluded null/nonpositive values. Assert both p95 and unchanged average/response behavior. Run node --test tests/provider-sla-p95.test.mjs tests/bazaar-health-query-errors.test.mjs. No open PR changes this route. work on the assigned branch you are on. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflow, package.json, or auth changes.
